title: Finance terms
disclaimer: Definitions reused from openly licensed and public-domain sources (credited on each term). Not official DECA content.
notes: NC flag: some sources are CC BY-NC 4.0 or CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (see sources). They are used only because DECA Masters is free and non-commercial (no ads, no paid tier, no sponsorship that makes it commercial). If that changes, these terms must come out.
ShareAlike: terms from CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 sources, including any adapted versions, must be shared under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

Communication: Fundamentals for the Workplace keeps its glossary as Pressbooks glossary entries. source.url points to the chapter that uses the term (or the book home page when no chapter links it); the definition text itself is in the book's public glossary data (see sources[].glossaryData).

Public-domain US federal sources (SEC Investor.gov, BLS, USPTO, FDIC, CFPB): credited as the agencies ask; no seals or logos; no endorsement implied. US-specific facts (laws, agencies, figures) are US context, not Canadian.
Every definition is copied from its source glossary (HTML tags removed). Any trim or correction is marked source.adapted = true and named after "Adapted:" in the attribution.
76 OpenStax glossary terms for this exam are held in _hold-openstax/vocab/finance.json until OpenStax grants permission (SOURCES.md section 1.2). They are not in this file.

terms.definition: Any tangible or intangible item that has value in an exchange. A bank account, a home, or shares of stock are all examples of assets.

source.title: Investor.gov Glossary: Asset
source.attribution: Definition from "Asset," Investor.gov glossary, U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/glossary/asset. Public domain (US federal work).

terms.definition: An amount owed to a person or organization for borrowed funds. Loans, notes, bonds, and mortgages are forms of debt. These different forms all call for borrowers to pay back the amount they owe, typically with interest, by a specific date, which is set forth in the repayment terms.

source.title: Investor.gov Glossary: Liability/Debt
source.attribution: Definition from "Liability/Debt," Investor.gov glossary, U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/glossary/liabilitydebt. Public domain (US federal work).

terms.definition: The profit earned by a company after all expenses and taxes have been deducted from revenue. A simple way to think about net income is it’s the price of a widget multiplied by the number of widgets sold (this result is revenue) minus the cost to make and sell the widgets, other expenses and any interest or taxes.

source.title: Investor.gov Glossary: Net Income
source.attribution: Definition from "Net Income," Investor.gov glossary, U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/glossary/net-income. Public domain (US federal work).

terms.definition: The total amount of money, or gross income, generated by a company from selling its goods and services. A simple way to think about revenue is it’s the price of a widget multiplied by the number of widgets sold.

source.title: Investor.gov Glossary: Revenue
source.attribution: Definition from "Revenue," Investor.gov glossary, U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/glossary/revenue. Public domain (US federal work).

terms.definition: A public company's net profit divided by the number of its common shares.

Earnings per share are calculated by dividing the earnings for the past 12 months by the number of common shares outstanding.
